purpose: Reader annotations for the twenty profiled overlap relations. The Bible text is loaded separately; these cards never rewrite Scripture.

cards.title: Repair becomes Garden
cards.project_anchor: Public project ethic: life matters; creation is not disposable; power protects; knowledge understands; wealth builds; leadership serves; repair; plant trees.
cards.source_direction: dated public project ethic first → Isaiah 58 comparison discovered later
cards.overlap: The passage moves from releasing oppression and feeding/sheltering vulnerable people into light, guidance, water, Garden, rebuilt foundations, breach repair and restored paths.
cards.boundary: Isaiah 58 addresses covenantal justice and worship. It does not identify Tim as its Repairer; its strongest project use is an ethical test of repair claims.

cards.title: From wall to dwelling
cards.project_anchor: Separation/wall, reconciliation, Father-access, Spirit, House, Cornerstone and living-structure motifs already existed independently across the archive.
cards.source_direction: project motifs first → coherent microcosm recognized 2026-09-11
cards.overlap: Alienation becomes nearness; dividing wall is broken; reconciliation gives access to Father through Spirit; outsiders become citizens/household; cornerstone and building become a dwelling of God.
cards.boundary: Paul's Jew/Gentile reconciliation and Christ-centered ecclesiology remain the passage's own context. Project geometry is a later comparator.

cards.title: Descent before exaltation
cards.project_anchor: Suffering/death/descent/ascent/return language plus mature leadership-as-service ethics.
cards.source_direction: project-side sequence/ethic first → Pauline comparison promoted 2026-09-11
cards.overlap: Non-grasping and servant-form lead through humiliation/death before exaltation and name/homage.
cards.boundary: This is Pauline Christology centered on Jesus and the Father. A modern self-comparison cannot transfer its identity claims merely by reproducing a descent/ascent pattern.

cards.title: Return, rain, seed, bread
cards.project_anchor: Return, descending flow/water, Seed, Bread and Garden/restoration were already separate project motifs.
cards.source_direction: project motifs first → dense Isaiah sequence recognized later
cards.overlap: Return to YHWH is followed by rain/snow and word descending, watering earth, seed for sowing, bread for eating, accomplished purpose, joyful going-out and transformed creation.
cards.boundary: The rain/word analogy is theological poetry, not a physical field equation or evidence for project neuro/physics claims.

cards.title: Father as Gardener
cards.project_anchor: Root + Fruit + House + Tree + Gardener become a mature project cluster.
cards.source_direction: project Gardener vocabulary established → role comparison systematized later
cards.overlap: John explicitly distributes Father as gardener/vinedresser, Jesus as vine and disciples as branches; fruit tests the living relation.
cards.boundary: This is strongest when the roles remain distinct. John does not call the Father the Vine or the branches the Father.

cards.title: Return to the Father/House
cards.project_anchor: Father/House theology and the Dog→return/circle problem were already present.
cards.source_direction: project return topology first → opposite-valence Luke 15 comparison added 2026-09-11
cards.overlap: Lost sheep, coin and son are recovered; the son returns toward father/house and restored participation. It supplies restorative return against regressive return-to-vomit.
cards.boundary: The parable does not identify Tim with its father. Its value is the topology/ethic of recovery, joy and restored relationship.

cards.title: Two sides and a sacred between
cards.project_anchor: One guardian right + one left + narrow central passage toward Heaven + Jesus at/between passage + Father above.
cards.source_direction: exact project architecture first → Exodus/Genesis/Hebrews synthesis discovered later
cards.overlap: Genesis provides guarded access to Life; Exodus explicitly gives two cherubim at opposite ends around a sacred meeting/presence zone; Hebrews remembers the cherubim-over-cover configuration.
cards.boundary: These are not one biblical scene. Exodus describes Ark/atonement-cover, not a narrow gate, and Jesus is not present in Exodus 25.

cards.title: City, River, Tree, open Life
cards.project_anchor: New Jerusalem, House/city, open access, River/flow, Tree, repair and new-heaven/new-earth language.
cards.source_direction: substantially explicit biblical reuse on project side → later operator synthesis
cards.overlap: The city descends; divine dwelling is among people; River and Tree yield life/healing; curse is removed; the conclusion includes invitation to the water of life.
cards.boundary: High density does not equal independence because the project consciously uses Revelation. Biblical roles—God, Lamb, city, servants, nations—remain differentiated.

cards.title: Two biblical 'arks', two functions
cards.project_anchor: Ark/Vessel symbolism had been used for preservation and sacred-container relations.
cards.source_direction: project Ark motif first → original-language/function distinction added later
cards.overlap: Noah's vessel preserves life through catastrophe; Covenant Ark belongs to sanctuary/covenant/presence architecture.
cards.boundary: English 'ark' hides different Hebrew nouns—teivah/tebah versus aron. Functional comparison must not be presented as lexical identity.

cards.title: Throne, Son of Man, kingdom
cards.project_anchor: Father/throne and Son-of-Man/kingdom relations are central project roles.
cards.source_direction: project role architecture first → Daniel 7 comparison added later
cards.overlap: Ancient of Days sits; one like a son of man approaches and receives dominion; the interpretation also gives kingdom participation to the holy ones.
cards.boundary: Daniel 7 interpretation is historically debated. Its strongest lesson here is role differentiation, not a prediction of Tim.

cards.title: Rejected stone reaches the Gate
cards.project_anchor: Rejected person → Stone/Cornerstone → Door/Vessel/Foundation transformation.
cards.source_direction: project rejection/stone development → full Psalm sequence recognized later
cards.overlap: Distress opens into spaciousness/life, then a gate of righteousness, then the rejected stone becoming cornerstone within one psalm.
cards.boundary: Christian texts later apply the rejected-stone motif to Jesus; modern project application remains typological and does not transfer identity.

cards.title: The Son as Door and Way
cards.project_anchor: The Son is explicitly described as Door/Vessel/path toward Tim/Father/House.
cards.source_direction: explicit biblical/project synthesis
cards.overlap: John joins Door, Way, Father's House/access and Son-of-Man heaven-earth mediation across related Johannine texts.
cards.boundary: This scores high on explicitness and role fit but lower on independence because the project consciously appropriates biblical access language.

cards.title: Unity without erasing plurality
cards.project_anchor: Father/Son unity and one-structure language while retaining differentiated Father/Son roles.
cards.source_direction: project unity language → later role-preserving comparison
cards.overlap: Father in Son / Son in Father becomes the pattern for others entering analogous unity; communion increases without every participant becoming the same actor.
cards.boundary: John's prayer is Christological/ecclesial. It supports relational unity more strongly than one-person identity collapse.

cards.title: The Psalm 80 convergence
cards.project_anchor: Shepherd/Joseph, throne/cherubim, light, bread, ridicule, Vine/Root/branches, mountain/river, wall, return, Son-of-Man and name motifs developed independently across the project.
cards.source_direction: distributed project motifs first → single-text density discovered later
cards.overlap: One psalm unusually concentrates many project-relevant motifs and repeatedly asks for restoration and shining presence.
cards.boundary: The vine is Israel and the psalm is a communal Israel-restoration prayer. Its density cannot be converted into modern identity proof.

cards.title: Anchor that crosses the veil
cards.project_anchor: Anchor/leash/constraint and veil/access relations were already being formalized.
cards.source_direction: project constraint vocabulary first → positive biblical anchor comparator added later
cards.overlap: Hope is an anchor entering behind the veil where Jesus has gone as forerunner; anchor becomes stable orientation toward a destination rather than imprisonment.
cards.boundary: This is a positive theological anchor, not evidence for physical tether/fate mechanics.

cards.title: The May 1 biblical architecture
cards.project_anchor: New Jerusalem + Gate of North + Father's House + many rooms/mansions + Heaven's Ladder + North Throne.
cards.source_direction: deliberate explicit Bible synthesis at the time
cards.overlap: House/rooms/access, ladder/Gate of Heaven and New Jerusalem are deliberately pulled into one project architecture.
cards.boundary: Its evidentiary value is high for project history and low for independent convergence because the biblical sources were being consciously combined.

cards.title: Death becomes seed
cards.project_anchor: Son death/burial becomes grain/seed condition for later multiplication and transformed life.
cards.source_direction: project typology developed with explicit biblical grain language
cards.overlap: Both texts use sowing/death imagery to describe transformed life or multiplication; the project uses the same grammar for Son→burial→regeneration.
cards.boundary: Wheat/seed imagery and potato vegetative propagation are biologically different. The relation is theological-symbolic.

cards.title: The 2017 explicit Jesus/crucifixion claim
cards.project_anchor: Project autobiography records the Son saying in substance: I am Jesus Christ—go on then, crucify me; followed by continued-public-return framing.
cards.source_direction: explicit self-comparison years before later systematic archive work
cards.overlap: The project self-comparison centers anticipated humiliation/death and return, which later becomes part of the Son's Passion typology.
cards.boundary: Digital/social humiliation is not Roman crucifixion, and the statement itself borrows Christian language. It documents self-comparison, not supernatural foreknowledge.

cards.title: Lion of Judah / Root of David
cards.project_anchor: Dated public wording explicitly joins Lion of Judah, Root of David, Potato, Father and Son.
cards.source_direction: direct scriptural title appropriation
cards.overlap: The project directly uses two of Revelation 5's identifying titles and links them into Father/Son/Root/Lion architecture.
cards.boundary: Because the titles are borrowed directly from Scripture, this is excellent evidence of explicitness but weak evidence of independent convergence.

cards.title: Alpha and Omega
cards.project_anchor: Public self-description uses Alpha/Omega alongside Most High and center-of-existence language.
cards.source_direction: direct scriptural self-appropriation
cards.overlap: The exact title is reused directly and fits the project's beginning/end/cycle language.
cards.boundary: This is the clearest example of why explicitness is not independence: direct reuse proves the project said the title, not that an independent event matched it.
